title: Sending a file need not pass through your program
body: Copying a file to a socket the naive way hauls bytes disk-to-kernel-to-user-to-kernel-to-network. The sendfile call lets the kernel move data directly, so web servers stopped burning CPU on copies that added nothing. 'Zero-copy' really means zero unnecessary copies; the bytes still travel, the middleman retires.
source_hint: sendfile(2) man page and kernel documentation
